one_liner: An adult male with a right chronic subdural hematoma underwent successful right burr hole craniotomy for evacuation and subdural drain placement under general anesthesia, and was transported to PACU in satisfactory condition.

procedures.name: Right burr hole craniotomy for evacuation of subdural hematoma and placement of subdural drain
procedures.outcome: There was egress of a large amount of liquid. Under pressure, we irrigated for quite sometime until irrigation was returning mostly clear.

course.narrative: The patient was brought to the operating room and placed in the supine position under general endotracheal anesthesia. A right shoulder roll was placed and the head was turned to the left. The scalp was prepped and draped. Incisions were marked and the parietal boss incision was opened. A bur hole was fashioned, widened, and the dura was coagulated and opened, revealing a large amount of liquid under pressure. Thorough irrigation was performed until clear. A subdural drain was placed in the subdural space and secured. The wound was closed with Vicryl sutures and staples, and a sterile dressing was applied. The patient was extubated in the OR and transported to the PACU in satisfactory condition.
